# W4 OVERHEAD SCALING

**Generated by:** `tests/performance/benchmark_overhead_scaling.py`

Estimator: **minimum of 5 per-repeat medians**, for both baseline and
instrumented. Contention can only add time, so the minimum is the cleanest
physically impossible result (the instrumented run appearing faster than baseline).

## Why this exists

The headline overhead benchmark runs a tiny model whose step takes about 5 ms.
A fixed per-step cost is therefore a large percentage of it. That leaves a
question which must be answered by measurement rather than by extrapolation:

> Is the percentage failure a property of the debugger, or of the toy baseline?

## Answer

| Workload | Baseline | core metrics | **core added** | T1 layer hooks | **T1 added** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tiny (4L, d32) | 4.66 ms | 5.14 ms | **+0.47 ms (+10.2 %)** | 5.18 ms | **+0.51 ms (+11.0 %)** |
| medium (8L, d128) | 18.39 ms | 19.09 ms | **+0.69 ms (+3.8 %)** | 19.35 ms | **+0.95 ms (+5.2 %)** |
| large (12L, d256) | 44.76 ms | 44.81 ms | **+0.05 ms (+0.1 %)** | 44.96 ms | **+0.19 ms (+0.4 %)** |

### Budget verdict per workload

| Workload | core < 3 % | T1 < 8 % |
|---|---|---|
| tiny (4L, d32) | FAIL (+10.2 %) | FAIL (+11.0 %) |
| medium (8L, d128) | FAIL (+3.8 %) | PASS (+5.2 %) |
| large (12L, d256) | PASS (+0.1 %) | PASS (+0.4 %) |

Across a 10x range of baseline step time (4.66 ms to 44.76 ms):

* core-metric overhead fell from +10.2 % to +0.1 %
* T1 layer-hook overhead fell from +11.0 % to +0.4 %

The overhead is a **mix** of a fixed per-step term (event construction, emission,
validation) and a term proportional to parameter count (the norm reductions). The
norm reductions cannot go below one memory-bandwidth pass over the parameters, so
they scale with the model but *not* with how long the step takes. A larger model
with the same step duration would therefore show a higher percentage; a larger
model with a proportionally longer step would not.

## p95

| Workload | Baseline p95 | core p95 | T1 p95 |
|---|---|---|---|
| tiny (4L, d32) | 4.91 ms | 5.59 ms | 6.49 ms |
| medium (8L, d128) | 19.12 ms | 20.55 ms | 22.42 ms |
| large (12L, d256) | 47.77 ms | 48.95 ms | 54.18 ms |

## What is still NOT verified

* **A production-scale model.** The largest workload here is 12 layers at
  d_model 256 -- far smaller than an LLM in training. Extrapolating to a
  multi-second step is **not** a measurement and is not claimed.
* **A GPU.** All measurements are CPU/MPS on an Apple M2 Max. On CUDA the
  balance shifts: `global_gradient_norm` reduces over device tensors, so its
  cost depends on interconnect and on how many syncs remain (currently one).
* **Distributed.** Single process only.
